episodes.summary: in this solo episode, sadie explains why asking for help feels so overwhelming—especially when you're already struggling with your mental health. she walks through the psychological barriers that keep us from being vulnerable (fear of making it real, lack of vocabulary, shame, low self-worth) and shares how she learned to open up to her parents during treatment. the episode introduces exposure therapy for vulnerability: practicing small, doable acts of honesty instead of forcing yourself into big emotional conversations. sadie offers concrete techniques like naming emotions mid-conversation, body doubling with friends, and journaling as low-stakes ways to build the skill of asking for help. listeners come away with a practical roadmap for getting more comfortable being seen when they're not at their best.

episodes.summary: sadie talks with dr. scott barry kaufman, a psychologist and columbia professor, about why gen z's college experience feels so different. they cover how students today are dealing with more apathy and less hope than a decade ago, how constant phone and laptop use pulls people out of the moment, and what ai means for learning and cheating. dr. kaufman explains how standardized tests favor one kind of mind and why it's okay to rewrite the rules and find your own path — whether that's community college, a trade, or skipping college altogether. the conversation is honest about the struggles gen z faces and realistic about when you have to play the game versus when you can define success for yourself.

episodes.title: 250. why high achievers still struggle with mental health

episodes.summary: sadie answers a listener question about maintaining mental health while pursuing ambitious goals in college and beyond. she shares that mental health must remain a foundation even when you're thriving, not just in crisis. the episode covers how to design your life so routines (sleep, relationships, movement, nutrition) sustain you without relying on willpower, how to audit your week to see if you're progressing or regressing, and why offloading mental health needs into habits keeps you on an upward trajectory. sadie emphasizes that without your mental health, you have nothing—and that's especially true for high achievers.

episodes.title: 249. what to do during a panic attack (when nothing else works!!)
episodes.excerpt: if you struggle with panic attacks and haven’t found a way to stop them, this episode will change that completely! in this solo episode, i share my psychology-backed hack to end 100% of your panic attacks. by the end of this episode, you’ll have a mental health skill in your toolbox designed for…
episodes.summary: sadie shares a psychology-backed dbt skill called the ice dive that stops panic attacks by activating your mammalian diving reflex. she explains why panic attacks make your body feel out of control (your sympathetic nervous system takes over), how the ice dive physically lowers your heart rate and breathing rate by signaling to your brain that you're drowning, and practical ways to use it—from a bowl of ice water at home to cool paper towels in a public bathroom. this skill works 100% of the time because it taps into a physiological response, making it reliable even when other coping strategies lose effectiveness.

episodes.title: 248. why “look on the bright side” doesn’t work (do THIS instead!)
episodes.excerpt: if you struggle with depression, you might be facing a brain bias that’s stopping you from healing. this solo episode explains how your brain is holding you back and why daily diaries can move your mental health forward. by the end of this episode, you’ll know the three easy aspects of your mental…

episodes.summary: sadie unpacks how to tell if you need therapy or if what you're experiencing is just a normal part of life. drawing on her work diagnosing depression and anxiety, she explains the two key signs: distress (does this feel unsustainable?) and impairment (is this getting in the way of your daily life?). she shares what she learned from hitting rock bottom with suicidal depression—that waiting until things are unbearable makes recovery so much harder. listeners learn three questions to ask themselves when deciding if it's time to get help, and why building skills early matters more than waiting for a crisis.

episodes.title: 224. stop ‘shoulding’ + shaming yourself

episodes.summary: sadie opens up about her ongoing struggle with sleep and how she caught herself in a harmful 'should' mentality—believing she should be able to maintain a consistent sleep schedule without extra support, even though resources and scaffolding are available to her. she unpacks the psychology of shame versus guilt, explains how shame can block us from accepting help and reaching our goals, and shares dbt skills for recognizing when shame doesn't fit the facts. the episode walks through opposite action techniques, the importance of self-forgiveness, and how to stop getting in our own way when we need support.

episodes.title: 223. no one tells you this career advice (how to *actually* get ahead at work) feat. dr. rosalind chow
episodes.excerpt: Today…

episodes.summary: sadie sits down with dr. rosalind chow, an organizational behavior professor at carnegie mellon, to talk about mentorship, sponsorship, and navigating workplace inequality. they break down the difference between mentors (who help you grow) and sponsors (who advocate for you to others), why sponsorship matters for women and people of color, and how to build these relationships without feeling like you have nothing to offer. dr. chow also explains why structural change is so hard, how to talk about inequality without triggering defensiveness, and why celebrating others' strengths—instead of comparing yourself—is the real skill that sets you up for long-term success.

episodes.title: 221. two psych majors tell ALL: GPAs, grad school, & so much more!
episodes.excerpt: In this week’s episode, we are sharing part two of our tips for being a psychology major! I am once again joined by my friend (and fellow psych major at UPenn!) to discuss even more things you absolutely need to know about majoring in psychology in college.
guests: olivia, upenn psychology major and president of penn undergraduate psychology society
episodes.summary: sadie and her friend olivia, both graduating psychology majors at upenn, share part two of their advice for psych students. they discuss how much grades really matter (especially in-major gpa), choosing meaningful extracurriculars over fomo, getting involved in research early, and applying for small grants even as undergrads. they cover practical steps like building a cv from day one, writing a thesis, presenting posters at conferences, and networking by providing value first. both applied to grad school senior year (unusual but worth it for the experience) and emphasize that success in psychology comes more from what you do outside the classroom—research, volunteering, mentorship—than from coursework alone.

episodes.title: 220. how to succeed as a psychology major (& what we wish we knew sooner)
episodes.excerpt: In this week’s episode, I am joined by one of my closest friends at UPenn to discuss one of our favorite topics: being a psych major! guests: olivia nicastro
episodes.summary: sadie and her close friend olivia, both graduating psychology majors at upenn, share everything they wish they'd known before choosing psychology as their major. they break down what psych classes are actually like (hint: lots of reading you won't do all of, test-based intros, and seminar-style upper levels), explain why research experience is essential even if you want to be a clinician, and give a realistic timeline for undergrads. they also discuss how to find the right research lab, what questions to ask mentors, green and red flags in labs, and how to balance workload without burning out. plus: their favorite classes, why you need stats over calc, and a detour into wild moral dilemmas.

episodes.title: 219: feeling like you don’t belong in school is the norm… let’s change it feat. dr. greg walton

guests: dr. greg walton, michael forman university fellow and professor of psychology at stanford university
episodes.summary: sadie talks with dr. greg walton, stanford psychology professor, about belonging in school and how small interventions can shift outcomes. they cover stereotype threat (how negative stereotypes disrupt performance), the belonging intervention (storytelling that reframes struggles as normal and temporary), and why mentor relationships matter so much. dr. walton explains how his research shows that helping students see early difficulties as part of everyone's transition—not a sign they don't belong—leads to better grades, stronger relationships, and healthier lives years later. they also discuss gen z's mental health crisis, the value of honest conversations that don't pathologize struggle, and how everyone belongs more when everyone feels they belong.

episodes.title: 218: is social media causing the mental health crisis?! (probably not) feat. dr. emily weinstein

episodes.title: 217. mental health book club series: lost connections by johann hari
episodes.excerpt: In this week's solo episode, I am sharing one of my absolute favorite mental health books as a part of my new book club series! This week's pick is Lost Connections by Johann Hari, a New York Times bestselling book that explores what truly causes (and fixes!) depression.
episodes.summary: sadie breaks down lost connections by johann hari, a book exploring why we get depressed and how to find hope. she covers the chemical imbalance theory (debunking the idea that depression is just a serotonin issue), johann's nine causes of depression (disconnection from meaningful work, relationships, values, childhood trauma, status, nature, and the future), and how depression is often a signal that something in your life isn't working. listeners walk away with a new framework for understanding depression as a normal response to abnormal circumstances, plus concrete ways to reconnect and address root causes instead of just medicating symptoms.

episodes.title: 216. your 20s are for healing childhood wounds feat. kelly u
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Kelly Uchima—a passionate Asian American mental health advocate and wellness content creator, named Health and Wellness Influencer of the Year by the Influence Agency in 2023. As a sought-after speaker at events hosted by Meta, Samsung, VidCon, and Reese Witherspoon’s Hello…
guests: kelly uchima, asian american mental health advocate and wellness content creator
episodes.summary: sadie talks with kelly uchima, an asian american mental health advocate, about healing from childhood trauma in your twenties. they cover struggling with disordered eating and mental health challenges from a young age, working through codependent and narcissistic relationships, and learning to set boundaries with family. kelly shares how she became sober from weed after years of using it to numb her feelings, and how she's building a healthier relationship with her body and gut health issues. the conversation emphasizes that healing isn't linear—you don't have to have it all figured out, but you can choose differently each day.

episodes.title: 215. i interviewed my THERAPIST?!! validation, dbt, stigma + more feat. dr. caroline fleck
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Dr. Caroline Fleck—a licensed psychologist, corporate consultant, author, and an Adjunct Clinical Instructor at Stanford University. guests: dr. caroline fleck
episodes.summary: sadie interviews her therapist, dr. caroline fleck, about validation and why it's so crucial for gen z mental health. they discuss how dbt balances acceptance and change, why chronic invalidation leads to mental health struggles, and how validation differs from praise or approval. dr. fleck explains eight ways to validate someone, why we self-invalidate, and how to support loved ones in crisis without reinforcing harmful behaviors. they also talk about turning suffering into meaning, navigating the gen z mental health crisis, and why seeking validation (not approval) from others is actually healthy.

episodes.title: 214. unfiltered college advice: social anxiety, burnout, school stress, + more
episodes.excerpt: In this week's solo episode, I am once again reacting to mental health posts on Reddit! I poured through TONS of Reddit posts on different mental health challenges people are experiencing in college and shared my most unfiltered responses to them.
episodes.summary: sadie reacts to mental health posts from reddit, focusing on common college struggles. she covers navigating group projects when others don't contribute (communicate in writing, keep receipts, talk to your professor), balancing workload and social life (something has to give—know your priorities and what's sustainable), feeling lonely despite being around people (it takes 50–200 hours to build close friendships, give yourself grace), and what freshmen should know before starting college (find a mentor, join a lab early if you're a psych major, sleep only in your room). she emphasizes that college is the first time many people are responsible for their own mental health—eating well, sleeping consistently, moving your body, and planning positive moments—and that's hard without the structure and support system of high school.

episodes.title: 213. breaking through struggle & self-doubt feat. john r. miles
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is John R. Miles — a f ormer U.S. Na vy officer, Fortune 50 senior executive, entrepreneur, author, and award-winning podcast host. He is a recognized expert on intentional behavior change, leadership, personal mastery, and the transformative power of "mattering."

episodes.title: 212. how to be more resilient feat. dr. glenn schiraldi
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Glenn R. Schiraldi. guests: dr. glenn schiraldi, founder of resilience training international
episodes.summary: sadie talks with dr. glenn schiraldi, founder of resilience training international, about what makes us resilient and how childhood experiences shape our stress responses. they cover ace scores (adverse childhood experiences), the difference between good stress and toxic stress, and why talk therapy alone often doesn't work for early trauma. dr. schiraldi shares specific skills for regulating stress—like five-minute breathing exercises and body-based techniques—and explains treatments like accelerated resolution therapy that help rewire trauma in the brain. the conversation includes how to find trauma specialists, why shame gets imprinted in the nonverbal brain, and how self-esteem skills can build the kind of resilience that helps you absorb stress without losing yourself.

episodes.title: 211. grit (I took angela duckworth's class at upenn)
episodes.excerpt: In this week's solo episode, I discuss everything I learned in my Grit Lab course as a psychology major at the University of Pennsylvania. This class is taught by Dr. Angela Duckworth , a Penn professor, researcher, MacArthur fellow, and best-selling author. This episode is your condensed guide on…
episodes.summary: sadie shares everything she learned in dr. angela duckworth's grit lab course at upenn. she breaks down what grit actually is (sustained passion and perseverance for long-term goals), how it differs from self-control, and why it predicts success better than talent. she walks through goal hierarchies, the rubicon model for goal-setting, deliberate practice, and practical strategies like goal fusion and the three boxes model. the episode condenses a semester of psychology research into actionable takeaways on aligning your daily actions with your values, setting effective goals, and becoming an expert through effort.

episodes.title: 210. why you’re feeling suicidal + a therapist’s advice on how to cope feat. kathryn gordon
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Kathryn Gordon — a l icensed clinic al psychologist, speaker, and author. She specializes in cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and has written several books on using CBT skills to prevent suicide.

episodes.summary: sadie talks with dr. kathryn gordon, a clinical psychologist specializing in cbt for suicide prevention, about why people have suicidal thoughts and how to cope with them. they cover what prompts suicidal ideation (feeling like a burden, isolated, or in hopeless pain), why it feels impossible to do helpful things when you're struggling, and how to talk about suicide openly without shame. kathryn walks through cbt tools like identifying thought patterns, reframing beliefs, and building a safety plan with distraction skills and environmental changes. she also explains what peers can do to support friends—listen non-judgmentally, encourage professional help, and set boundaries—without taking on responsibility they can't handle.

episodes.title: 209. How to Set Habits You'll ACTUALLY Use [Solo]
episodes.excerpt: In this week's solo episode, I discuss how to set healthy habits and achieve your goals this year using psychology! I'll be sharing my favorite psychology hacks on how to set achievable habits and goals before diving into my personal goals for 2025.
episodes.summary: sadie breaks down the psychology of habit formation and goal setting for the new year. she explains the difference between motivation (why we do things) and volition (how we do them), shares research-backed frameworks like the woop method and implementation intentions, and walks through why willpower alone doesn't work. the episode covers how to set effective goals, build sustainable habits through cues and rewards, and break bad patterns by changing your environment. sadie also shares her personal 2025 goals around sleep consistency, daily steps, posting more on social media, running regularly, and practicing social exposure therapy.

episodes.title: 208. How to Be a Mental Health ADVOCATE feat. Active Minds
episodes.excerpt: Today's guests are Alison Malmon and Lauren Cikara of Active Minds , the nation’s le ading nonprofit organization promoting mental health awareness and education for young adults. episodes.summary: sadie sits down with alison malmon and lauren cikara of active minds to talk about mental health advocacy. alison shares how losing her brother to suicide in college led her to start active minds at penn and why the stigma around mental health prevents people from getting help early. they discuss active minds' a.s.k. framework (acknowledge, support, keep in touch) for everyday peer support, warning signs to watch for in friends or teens, and how to start an active minds chapter. the conversation also covers policy priorities like increasing diverse mental health providers, embedding mental health into school culture and other social issues, and treating mental health with the same urgency as physical safety.

episodes.title: 207. What Research Says About DEPRESSION feat. Dr. Steven Hollon
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Dr. Steven D. Hollon— the Gertrude Conaway Vanderbilt Professor of Psychology at Vanderbilt University. guests: dr. steven hollon, professor of psychology at vanderbilt university
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with dr. steven hollon, a leading depression researcher at vanderbilt, to talk about what the science actually tells us about depression. they cover how common depression really is (way more than we thought), why it might be an evolved response rather than just a broken brain, and what makes cognitive behavioral therapy so effective. dr. hollon explains why some people have one depressive episode while others have many, why adolescence is such a vulnerable time, and two practical things anyone can do when depression hits: don't wait to feel like doing something before you do it, and don't believe everything you think. the conversation is research-heavy but accessible, offering real clarity on how depression works and what helps.

episodes.title: 206. EMOTION REGULATION: Misophonia, DBT, Reactivity, & More feat. Dr. Mark Zachary Rosenthal
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Dr. Mark Zachary Rosenthal —a clinical psychologist and an Associate Professor in the Psychiatry & Behavioral Sciences department and the Psychology & Neuroscience department at Duke University. grace heppes, outreach and education coordinator at the duke center for misophonia and emotion regulation
episodes.summary: sadie visits duke university to talk with dr. mark zachary rosenthal and grace heppes about emotion regulation, dbt, and misophonia. dr. rosenthal explains how emotions work—why we feel them, what happens in our bodies, and why some people struggle more with regulating them. he breaks down what makes dbt unique, from its team-based approach to how therapists stay supported, and offers a practical tip for finding quality dbt care. grace shares her lived experience with misophonia, describing the isolation, invalidation, and daily challenges she faced growing up, and how advocacy and research are finally changing the landscape. together they discuss the dialectic of accommodating misophonia: systems need to do better, but individuals also need tools to cope with a world that won't always accommodate them.

episodes.title: 205. What I Wish I Knew About Anxiety...
episodes.excerpt: In this week's solo episode, I discuss what I wish I'd known when struggling with anxiety. Through my lived experiences with anxiety as well as my psychology coursework and academic research, I've collected a lot of tips on how to manage anxiety.
episodes.summary: in this solo episode, sadie shares what she wishes she'd known when struggling with anxiety, drawing from her lived experience and psychology coursework. she covers how to understand anxiety's evolutionary purpose, why avoidance makes it worse, and practical skills like exposure therapy and the tip skill (temperature, intense exercise, paced breathing, paired muscle relaxation). listeners learn dbt and cbt tools for both short-term panic attacks and long-term management, plus why a little anxiety can actually help performance.

episodes.title: 204. Your Guide to Generational Trauma feat. Dr. Mariel Buqué

guests: dr. mariel buqué, psychologist and author of break the cycle: a guide to healing intergenerational trauma
episodes.summary: sadie talks with dr. mariel buqué about generational trauma—what it is, how it passes through families biologically and psychologically, and how it shows up differently for each person depending on their experiences. dr. buqué explains what it really means to break the cycle, how to navigate pushback from family members when you're doing this work, and why nervous system regulation has to come before digging into past wounds. listeners learn practical starting points: finding body attunement, creating co-healing partnerships, and sitting with yourself without distractions to understand your triggers.

episodes.title: 203. 5 Things You Didn't Know About Depression feat. Jonathan Rottenberg
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Jonathan Rottenberg— the director of the Better Outcomes Laboratory at Cornell University, which explores long-term functioning and well-being after depression and related conditions. guests: jonathan rottenberg, director of the better outcomes laboratory at cornell university
episodes.summary: sadie talks with jonathan rottenberg, a professor at cornell who studies depression and long-term outcomes. they discuss how depression actually changes the way people experience emotions—making them less reactive to external stimuli, both positive and negative. the conversation explores why depression rates are rising in young people, how our cultural expectations about emotions contribute to this, and the surprising finding that about 10% of people who've had depression go on to report very high levels of well-being. they also talk about post-traumatic growth, how depression can lead to meaningful life changes and skills, and why we need more nuanced conversations about what it's like to live through and after depression.

episodes.title: 202. 5 Ways to Form a Secure Attachment Style feat. Thais Gibson
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Thais Gibson —a best-selling author, counselor, speaker, and founder of The Personal Development School. Based on her scientific research, she created the Gibson Integrated Attachment Theory, which empowers individuals to heal different attachments in their lives and reprogram any…
guests: thais gibson, founder of the personal development school
episodes.summary: sadie talks with thais gibson, founder of the personal development school, about attachment theory and how our childhood experiences shape how we show up in relationships. they cover the four attachment styles (secure, anxious, dismissive avoidant, and fearful avoidant), what each one looks like, and where those patterns come from. thais walks through five concrete steps for moving toward secure attachment: reprogramming core fears, learning to meet your own needs, regulating your nervous system, setting boundaries, and communicating effectively. they also talk about supporting people with different attachment styles, how siblings can develop totally different patterns even in the same household, and what conscious parenting looks like during the teen years.

episodes.title: 201. The Science of Motivating Gen Z: Mentors, Purpose, and Politics feat. Dr. David Yeager
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is David Yeager— a professor of psychology at the University of Texas at Austin who is considered “one of the world’s leading experts” on the psychology of young people, according to the New York Times Magazine . episodes.summary: in this episode, sadie talks with dr. david yeager, a psychology professor at ut austin who studies motivation in young people. they dig into why traditional programs (dare, anti-smoking campaigns) backfire with teens, what makes the 10–25 brain so sensitive to social feedback, and how a "mentor mindset"—high standards plus genuine support—actually works. dr. yeager also shares tactical advice on finding mentors, receiving feedback without shutting down, and cultivating purpose now instead of waiting until you're "old enough" to matter. the conversation touches on election messaging, college pressure, and why the adult world's assumption that teens are incompetent is both wrong and harmful.

episodes.title: 200. Back to School Advice (DBT Edition)
episodes.excerpt: Happy episode 200!!! In this week's solo episode, I am sharing my favorite DBT skills and tricks that you can use to thrive in school.
episodes.summary: in this solo episode celebrating 200 episodes, sadie shares dbt skills and strategies for thriving during the school year. she walks through how to set meaningful goals and track habits using bullet journals, explains the abc skills (accumulate positives, build mastery, cope ahead) for emotion regulation, and emphasizes the importance of exposure therapy over avoidance. she gives practical examples from her own life—like improving her makeup routine or arranging flowers—to show how building mastery boosts self-esteem, and encourages listeners to plan positive moments (especially relationship-based ones) and face uncomfortable situations instead of withdrawing.

episodes.title: 199. Growing Pains: Advice for Teens & Parents on Navigating Teenage Years feat. Ellen Galinsky
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Ellen Galinsky— president of the Families and Work Institute and author of several popular books researching adolescents and teenagers, including the bestselling parenting guide, Mind in the Making, and her recently published work, The Breakthrough Years . guests: ellen galinsky, president of families and work institute and author of mind in the making and the breakthrough years
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with ellen galinsky, president of the families and work institute and author of the breakthrough years, to talk about what teens are actually going through. they cover the emotional realities of adolescence—the highs, lows, and constant transitions—and how adults often misunderstand or stereotype teens instead of seeing them as individuals. ellen shares research on purpose, autonomy, and the power of helping others, plus practical advice on how parents can listen without fixing and how teens can build the skills they need. the conversation also touches on navigating phones, mental health conversations, and finding people who make you feel like a good person.

episodes.title: 198. Chrysalis School Montana: My Troubled Teen Industry Experience
episodes.excerpt: In this week's solo episode, I am sharing for the first time what my experience in the troubled teen industry was like. I was enrolled in Chrysalis School Montana in 2018 while I was struggling with my mental health in high school, unaware that I was part of a larger system that takes advantage of…
episodes.summary: sadie shares her personal experience at chrysalis school montana, a therapeutic boarding school she attended in 2018–2019. she explains what therapeutic boarding schools are, why they're often ineffective, and walks through the red flags she encountered: forced custody transfers, restricted family contact, ambiguous treatment timelines, unqualified staff, and a culture that normalized harmful practices. she discusses the recent lawsuit against chrysalis involving staff sexual abuse and systemic failures to protect students, and offers guidance for other survivors on processing trauma and for parents seeking ethical mental health care. this episode provides specific insight into how the troubled teen industry operates and what distinguishes it from evidence-based treatment programs.

episodes.title: 197. Life After The Program feat. Netflix Director & TTI Survivor Katherine Kubler
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Katherine Kubler— a Los Angeles-based writer, director, and editor. She recently directed and executive produced the Netflix original documentary series The Program: Cons, Cults, and Kidnapping, which exposes the corruption and abuse of the troubled teen industry.
guests: katherine kubler, director, producer, and troubled teen industry survivor
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with katherine kubler, director of the netflix documentary *the program: cons, cults, and kidnapping* and a survivor of ivy ridge. they discuss katherine's decision to expose the troubled teen industry, the challenges survivors face in processing normalized abuse, and how finding abandoned program files validated their memories. katherine explains red flags in tti programs (restricted family contact, long-term residential mandates, lack of regulation), the rebranding from wasp to natsap, and the complete absence of evidence supporting these interventions. she shares what she's learned since the documentary aired—including that many wasp leaders still run programs today—and offers guidance for families seeking alternatives to residential treatment.

episodes.title: 196. EXPOSING the Troubled Teen Industry: How it Scams Parents & Harms Teens feat. Maia Szalavitz
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Maia Szalavitz— an award-winning author and journalist. guests: maia szalavitz, award-winning author and journalist
episodes.summary: this episode breaks down the troubled teen industry—a network of boot camps, wilderness programs, and boarding schools where abuse is the treatment. maia szalavitz, journalist and author of help at any cost, explains how these unregulated programs prey on scared parents, charge hospital prices for unlicensed staff, and leave survivors with ptsd, estrangement, and higher rates of suicide and overdose. she and sadie discuss why evidence-based care happens at home, what red flags to watch for, and how accountability models harm kids who need compassion. this is part one of a three-part series on the troubled teen industry.

episodes.title: 195. Your Family Vacation Survival Guide: Coping Skills, Boundaries, & More!
episodes.excerpt: In this week's solo episode, I talk about how to handle family vacations this summer. So, I share my favorite coping skills you can use to handle any challenges that come your…
episodes.summary: sadie shares practical skills for handling family vacations when they feel stressful or overwhelming. she talks about knowing your social battery as an introvert or extrovert, planning coping skills ahead of time (like stop, deep breathing, grounding), and how to set boundaries with family using dear man. she also covers why trips make you more emotionally vulnerable, how to check in during and after the trip, and why reinforcing positive moments helps everyone show up better next time. listeners learn concrete ways to recharge, communicate needs, and use distraction or grounding when anxiety or conflict comes up.

episodes.title: 194. Treating ADHD Without Medication: Tips to Improve Focus & Productivity feat. Dr. Nick Nissen
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Dr. Nick Nissen— a Harvard-trained psychiatrist, researcher, journalist, and expert in ADHD. In his concierge psychiatry practice, Nissen Clinic, he uses a suite of evidence-based treatments to get to the root of ADHD without using stimulant medications.
guests: dr. nick nissen, psychiatrist and adhd expert
episodes.summary: dr. nick nissen, a harvard-trained psychiatrist, breaks down adhd—what it actually is, how to tell if you have it, and how to treat it without relying on stimulants. he covers the pros and cons of medications like adderall, explains why so many people think they have adhd when they might not, and walks through practical skills anyone can use: calendar hygiene, task lists, cutting distractions, exercise, and motivation techniques. he also touches on supplements, diet tweaks, and the importance of accountability over just reading self-help books. whether you have adhd or just struggle to focus, this episode gives you concrete tools to get your executive functioning in shape.

episodes.title: 193. Gaining Wisdom & Weathering Grief in Your Twenties feat. Yasmine Cheyenne
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Yasmine Cheyenne— an author, TED TALK Motivational speaker, Air Force Veteran, and self-healing workshop leader who works to help people heal through traumatic situations. Through her work, she has guided corporate giants, including Google, NAMI, and Skillshare, and created The…
guests: yasmine cheyenne, author and self-healing workshop leader
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with yasmine cheyenne—author, motivational speaker, and self-healing workshop leader—to talk about navigating grief, leaning into your own wisdom, and setting boundaries in your twenties. yasmine shares what helped her through the loss of her grandmother, why acceptance and community were key, and how affirmations still play a role in her life. they also dig into the sugar jar metaphor for boundaries, what compassionate honesty means, and why it's okay to not have all the answers when life throws something new at you.

episodes.title: 192. Technology & Gen Z: AI, Cancel Culture, Ethics, & More feat. Nita Farahany

episodes.summary: sadie sits down with nita farahany, a law professor and expert on emerging tech ethics, to talk through how ai, neurotechnology, and social media are shaping gen z's sense of self. they cover how overconsumption of tech pushes us into autopilot thinking, how algorithms create echo chambers that fuel othering and cancel culture, and why gen z experiences speech differently than older generations—often as physical harm. nita explains the concept of self-determination (introspection, critical thinking, empathy) and how brain-tracking wearables could erode freedom of thought if we're not careful. she offers practical steps: opt out of personalized algorithms, use grayscale mode, exercise more, and advocate for user-level data controls.

episodes.title: 191. How Should We Talk About Depression? feat. Hans Schroder
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Hans Schroder— a Clinical Assistant Professor of Psychiatry at the University of Michigan Medical School and Adjunct Assistant Professor of Psychology at the University of Michigan who currently researches beliefs and messages about mental health and their impacts. As a licensed…
guests: dr. hans schroder, clinical assistant professor of psychiatry at the university of michigan
episodes.summary: sadie talks with dr. hans schroder, a clinical psychologist at the university of michigan, about how we talk about depression and why it matters. they cover the problems with the chemical imbalance theory, how believing depression is purely biological can reduce hope for recovery, and the idea that depression might be a signal that something in your life needs attention. hans shares research on how these beliefs affect people's willingness to engage in therapy and how identifying too strongly with a diagnosis can become limiting. they also discuss practical ways to validate someone's struggle while still encouraging agency and growth.

episodes.title: 190. How to Become an OPTIMIST: 3 Positive Psychology Techniques to Change Your Mindset

episodes.summary: sadie interviews madeline bailey, who holds an m.s. in neuroscience and researches trauma's impact on the brain. madeline shares how unaddressed trauma from her mom's mental health crisis in college led to depression, anxiety, and eventually a ptsd diagnosis—which sent her on a cross-country drive to process. she explains what happens in the brain during trauma (the amygdala, prefrontal cortex, and stress hormones), why some people develop ptsd (weakened connections between the prefrontal cortex and amygdala), and how timing matters (trauma during brain development has deeper effects). they discuss emotion regulation, emdr therapy, the role of rem sleep in processing trauma, and madeline's daily practices: self-compassion, meditation, therapy every two weeks, and pausing to sit with emotions instead of staying busy. listeners learn the science behind why healing is hard and why self-compassion is essential.

episodes.title: 87. Being the CEO of Your Life: Developing Leadership Skills, Taking Ownership, + Support Systems feat. Sarah Hernholm
episodes.excerpt: Today's guest is Sarah Hernholm—a former elementary school teacher turned entrepreneur and the founder of WIT. WIT (Whatever It Takes) works with t(w)eens around the world who are interested in using their voice and ideas to launch businesses, non-profits, and/or social movements. WIT also focuses…
guests: sarah hernholm, founder of wit
episodes.summary: sadie talks with sarah hernholm, founder of wit (whatever it takes), about taking ownership of your life like a ceo. they discuss why leadership skills matter for teens, how to shift from victim mindset to active ownership, and the connection between self-love and how you show up in the world. sarah shares practical steps: notice where you're using victim language, pick one promise you keep breaking to yourself and follow through, get clear on your values and mission statement, and be discerning about who's in your top five. they also talk about how your relationship with yourself shows up in your relationships with others, why hurt people hurt people, and how to build a support system that aligns with your values.

episodes.title: 86. The Teenage Girl's Guide to Increasing Confidence, Self-Esteem, and Self-Love feat. The Teen Life Coach, Sami Halvorsen
episodes.excerpt: Today I'm joined by Sami Halvorsen, the host of The Teen Life Coach podcast and the founder of Knowing Up. In this episode, Sami and I discuss her personal journey with self-love, the most common challenges teens struggle with, the importance of being proud of ourselves and celebrating little…
guests: sami halvorsen, founder of knowing up and host of the teen life coach podcast
episodes.summary: sadie and sami halvorsen, founder of knowing up and host of the teen life coach podcast, talk about building confidence and self-love as a teenager. they cover common struggles like anxiety about going to school, fear of saying the wrong thing, and comparing yourself to others. sami shares how self-confidence isn't about being perfect—it's about allowing yourself to feel awkward, vulnerable, and judged without running away. the conversation offers practical ways to celebrate small wins, lead your brain instead of letting it run the show, and start loving yourself even when things are hard.

episodes.title: 85. The Emotion Education you Should Have Gotten: Evolutionary Causes, Core Emotions, Primary vs. Secondary, and How to Cope
episodes.excerpt: Today I'm bringing you everything I learned from my time in treatment at 3East, McLean Hospital, and my multiple times through DBT about emotions! We go into a ton of depth on the evolutionary purpose of emotions, what can make it difficult to regulate emotions, primary vs. secondary emotions…
episodes.summary: sadie breaks down everything she learned about emotions from treatment at mclean hospital and dbt—the evolutionary purpose of emotions, what makes them hard to regulate, and the difference between primary and secondary emotions. she goes deep on the 10 core emotions (anger, disgust, envy, fear, happiness, jealousy, love, sadness, shame, guilt), explaining prompting events, interpretations, biological changes, expressions, and aftereffects for each. she wraps up with how to change emotional responses through checking the facts, opposite action, and problem-solving. it's a lot, but it's meant to be a resource you can return to when you need it.

episodes.title: 84. Andrea Arlington on Reparenting, Healing Generational Trauma, and Family Recovery
episodes.excerpt: In today's episode, I sit down with Andrea Arlington—ICF, PCC Life Coach Specializing in Family Recovery & Relationships. We discuss all things family recovery, generational trauma, reparenting and nurturing yourself so you can support others. If you're struggling with your family relationships…

episodes.title: 83. Freeing Yourself from Stress + Struggle by Understanding the Human Experience feat. Beth Segaloff
episodes.excerpt: Today’s guest is Beth Segaloff—a Licensed Clinical of Social Work, Life Coach, Reiki Master, Registered Yoga Teacher, Certified Firewalk Instructor, and Mom. We dive into the importance of approaching healing from a holistic perspective—mentally, physically, and spiritually, what happens when you…
guests: beth segaloff, licensed clinical social worker, life coach, reiki master, registered yoga teacher, certified firewalk instructor
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with beth segaloff—licensed clinical social worker, life coach, reiki master, yoga teacher, and certified firewalk instructor—to talk about healing from a holistic perspective. they discuss how lacking emotion education is for teens, what happens when you quiet your mind and practice mindfulness, and ways to incorporate those practices into daily life. beth shares her own journey through grief and trauma, explains how emdr works (including using it to strengthen positive emotions, not just reprocess trauma), and leads a guided meditation to help you center yourself and release tension.

episodes.title: 82. How to Let Go of Expectations + Improve Your Self-Talk feat. Paige Tonz
episodes.excerpt: Paige Tonz grew up in Peoria, AZ and began playing softball at 8 years old. She has competed at many levels; starting with rec ball, moving to club ball, and competing as a D1 athlete at Northwestern University. Her mission and goal are to help transform girls into strong women beyond the playing…
guests: paige tonz, girl athlete mindset mentor and former d1 softball player at northwestern
episodes.summary: paige tonz, a former d1 softball player and girls' mindset mentor, talks about shifting from result-based expectations to process-based ones—focusing on what you can control instead of outcomes like stats or grades. she shares how she struggled with perfectionism and fear of failure as an athlete, then found freedom her senior year by letting go of pressure. the conversation covers moving past mistakes, improving self-talk by writing down negative thoughts and reframing them, surrounding yourself with people who lift you up, and asking mentors for advice. paige emphasizes that negative thoughts are normal—the key is learning to navigate them so they don't control you.

episodes.title: 81. Dr. Aliza Pressman on Parenting Styles, Improving Parent-Child Relationships, and Navigating Conflict
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Dr. Aliza Pressman—a developmental psychologist with over 15 years of experience working with families. Dr. Aliza holds a BA from Dartmouth College, an MA in Risk, Resilience and Prevention from the Department of Human Development at Teacher’s College and her PhD in…
guests: dr. aliza pressman, developmental psychologist and co-founding director of the mount sinai parenting center
episodes.summary: sadie talks with dr. aliza pressman, a developmental psychologist, about how parenting styles shape parent-teen relationships. they cover the four main parenting styles (authoritative, authoritarian, permissive, neglectful) and why authoritative parenting—balancing sensitivity with clear boundaries—leads to healthier outcomes. dr. pressman explains how childhood emotional patterns follow us into adulthood, why we're drawn to familiar dynamics even when they're unhealthy, and how to navigate conflict without damaging trust. listeners learn practical steps for asking parents for what they need, repairing after arguments, and recognizing that all feelings are valid even when behaviors aren't.

episodes.title: 80. Surviving Teenage Depression + Anxiety: FAQs, Intensive Treatment, DBT, Coping Skills, + More
episodes.excerpt: In today's solo episode I tell my mental health story. I dive into my struggle with depression, anxiety, suicidal ideation, self-harm, and more. I also discuss my treatment journey, my experience with DBT, and where I'm at today. I give my best at-home mental health tips you can implement and…
episodes.summary: in this solo episode, sadie shares her full mental health story—from struggling with severe depression, anxiety, suicidal ideation, and self-harm starting in eighth grade, through four hospitalizations and trying countless treatments at home that didn't work. she walks through her 14-week stay at mclean hospital's intensive dbt program (three east), which finally changed everything when she decided she wanted to get better for herself. she explains what dbt is, how it saved her life, the core beliefs that fueled her suffering, and the small shifts (like sleep, self-compassion, and taking suicide off the table) that helped her heal. she also shares why she started the podcast and answers listener questions about relapse, shame, rock bottom, and what really made the difference in her recovery.

episodes.title: 79. Doug Bopst on Hitting Rock Bottom, Going From Felon to Fitness Coach, and Using Adversity to Your Advantage
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Doug Bopst—an award-winning personal trainer, author, speaker, and business owner. Those credentials and accolades are a result of his own transformation. He is a former felon and drug addict, sentenced to years in jail due to his poor decisions. He chose to use that time…
guests: doug bopst, personal trainer, author, and host of the adversity advantage podcast
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with doug bopst, a personal trainer, author, and speaker who transformed his life after incarceration. doug shares his journey from addiction and a felony conviction to building a career helping others through fitness. they discuss how he turned adversity into advantage, the deep connection between physical fitness and mental health, and practical steps for building sustainable habits. doug emphasizes personal accountability, starting small, and focusing on how far you've come rather than fixating on distant goals.

episodes.title: 78. Dr. Caroline Leaf on Neuroplasticity, the Brain vs. the Mind, and Cognitive Detoxing
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Dr. Caroline Leaf, a communication pathologist and cognitive neuroscientist specializing in cognitive and metacognitive neuropsychology. Since the early 1980s, she has researched the mind-brain connection, the nature of mental health, and the formation of memory. She was one…
guests: dr. caroline leaf, communication pathologist and cognitive neuroscientist
episodes.summary: sadie talks with dr. caroline leaf, a cognitive neuroscientist, about neuroplasticity—the brain's ability to change in response to how we use our mind. they discuss the difference between mind and brain, how childhood traumas physically wire into both brain and body, and why depression and anxiety aren't illnesses but emotional warning signals pointing to unprocessed experiences. dr. leaf walks through her neurocycle method: a five-step, 63-day process for identifying root causes, deconstructing toxic thought patterns, and rewiring the brain. listeners learn why quick fixes fail, how to become a 'thought detective,' and that healing takes time but is absolutely possible—no matter what you've been through.

episodes.title: 77. Dr. Kojo Sarfo on ADHD in Women: Presentations, Diagnosis, and Treatment
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Dr. Kojo Sarfo a social media content creator, mental health nurse practitioner, and psychotherapist to discuss all things ADHD. We dive into what is ADHD, how it presents different depending on age and gender, the ADHD diagnosis process, the treatment process, resources for…
guests: dr. kojo sarfo, mental health nurse practitioner and psychotherapist
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with dr. kojo sarfo, a mental health nurse practitioner and social media creator, to break down adhd in women and teens. they cover how adhd presents differently by gender and age, why women often go undiagnosed until their twenties or thirties, and what the diagnosis process actually looks like (spoiler: you don't always need expensive neuropsych testing). dr. sarfo walks through treatment options, practical daily habits that help manage symptoms, and how friends and parents can show up for someone with adhd. listeners walk away with a clearer picture of what adhd really is, how to recognize it, and where to find support.

episodes.title: 76. Dr. Alexandra Solomon on Building Healthy Relationships as a Teen, Exploring Sexuality, Soulmates, and Sex Education
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Dr. Alexandra Solomon a licensed clinical psychologist, author, and speaker, specializing in families, marriage, and relationships. She is a professor at Northwestern University and the author of Loving Bravely and Taking Sexy Back. In this episode, we dive into society’s…
guests: dr. alexandra solomon, licensed clinical psychologist, author, and professor at northwestern university
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with dr. alexandra solomon, a licensed clinical psychologist and professor at northwestern university who specializes in relationships and sexuality. they discuss how society sends different messages to boys and girls about sex and relationships, what makes a relationship healthy (trust, communication, low negativity threshold), and the difference between being sexual versus feeling sexualized. dr. solomon shares thoughts on soulmates, pornography's impact on teens, and how early relationship experiences shape our ability to build intimacy in adulthood. she emphasizes that sexuality develops best with self-compassion, body acceptance, and comprehensive sex education that goes beyond pregnancy prevention.

episodes.title: 75. Amen Clinic's Dr. Jay Faber on Teenage Substance Use: Brain Impacts, Long-Term Effects, and Quitting Tips
episodes.excerpt: This week's guest is Dr. Jay Faber. John A. “Jay” Faber, MD is a clinical and forensic double board-certified psychiatrist with more than three decades of experience in Child, Adolescent, and Adult Psychiatry. Currently, he is on the medical staff at the Amen Clinics in Encino, CA. We discuss…
guests: dr. jay faber, child psychiatrist at amen clinics
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with dr. jay faber, a child psychiatrist at amen clinics, to talk about adolescent substance use—specifically nicotine, alcohol, and marijuana. they cover what each substance does to the developing teenage brain, both short-term and long-term, and how to know when use becomes a problem. dr. faber shares practical advice on quitting (including the difference between long-term, medium-term, and short-term goals), red flags to watch for, and how parents can support a teen who's trying to quit. he also explains why vaping isn't necessarily safer than smoking, what makes nicotine so addictive, and how finding purpose and peer support are key to staying sober.

episodes.title: 74. Sophie Gray (Founder of DiveThru) on Diet Culture, Body Neutrality, Teenage Self-Harm, and Mental Health Education
episodes.excerpt: This week's guest is Sophie Gray. In this episode, Sophie and I dive deep into overcoming eating disorders, depression…
guests: sophie gray (founder of divethru)
episodes.summary: sadie talks with sophie gray, founder of the mental health app divethru. sophie shares her journey through teenage depression, self-harm, suicide attempts, and an eating disorder that began after bullying in her early teens. she explains how her mental health breakdown eventually led her to create divethru, which offers free journal prompts, mood trackers, and courses on specific challenges like adhd or navigating homophobic comments. they discuss body neutrality, diet culture, and why learning what's physically happening during anxiety or panic attacks is so empowering. sophie also shares the boundaries and habits—like power walking, deleting work apps after hours, and letting go of productivity shame—that help her maintain her mental health now.

episodes.title: 73. Victoria Garrick on Student-Athlete Mental Health, Body Image, Intuitive Eating, Vulnerability, and College Lifestyle
episodes.excerpt: This week's guest is former D1 Athlete, Victoria Garrick. episodes.summary: sadie talks with victoria garrick, a former d1 volleyball player at usc, about her experiences with performance anxiety, depression, and taking a mental health leave from her team. they discuss how student-athletes can prioritize mental health alongside their sport, the challenges of transitioning to college at 18, and how victoria shifted from struggling with binge eating and restricting to intuitive eating. victoria shares what helped her heal her relationship with food and body image, plus practical tips on managing burnout, staying honest about your limits, and making time for genuine connection.

episodes.title: 72. Almost 30's Krista Williams on How Meditation Will Change Your Life, Body Acceptance, Experiencing Your Emotions, and Surviving Depression + Anxiety
episodes.excerpt: Today I am sitting down with Krista Williams from Almost 30 for one of my all-time favorite interviews! We dive into Krista's experience with depression + anxiety and how she healed from this. Topics covered include trauma work, meditation, exploring sobriety, body acceptance, experiencing…
guests: krista williams from almost 30
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with krista williams from the almost 30 podcast to talk about navigating depression and anxiety in your teens and twenties. krista shares how unprocessed trauma and emotions fueled her mental health struggles, and how practices like meditation, exploring sobriety, and trauma therapy helped her heal. they discuss the shift from believing you are your emotions to understanding they're temporary signals, the importance of feeling instead of numbing, and how finding purpose through almost 30 changed krista's life. listeners walk away with insight on body acceptance, setting boundaries in relationships, and daily practices to maintain mental wellness.

episodes.title: 71. 1st Month of College DEBRIEF: Tips for Move-In, Socializing, Productivity, Studying, and more!
episodes.excerpt: So many fun interviews coming in the next few months, I wanted to sit down and give a life update before those get posted! In this ep, I talk all about my recent move to the University of Pennsylvania, orientation, starting classes, study skills that have been working habits to set yourself up for…
episodes.summary: sadie recaps her first month at the university of pennsylvania, covering move-in, orientation, and the start of classes. she shares what helped her adjust—setting up a comforting dorm, honoring her need to recharge before socializing, building a daily routine with coffee and library time, and giving herself compassion around making friends. she also talks through managing the freshmen plague (a non-covid cold), staying on top of coursework with notion and bullet journaling, and letting go of fomo. listeners take away practical advice for navigating big transitions while protecting their mental health.

episodes.title: 69. Navigating Anxiety as a Teenager: Coping Skills, Listener Q+A, Personal Experiences, and More
episodes.excerpt: Hello from Denmark (though I’m actually editing and releasing this 2 weeks later back at home) which is statistically the happiest country in the world. I dive into the Danish practices that contribute to such strong mental health and how you can implement these in your life. Onto the main…
episodes.summary: sadie covers navigating anxiety as a teenager, starting with insights from denmark (the world's happiest country) on practices that support mental health. she breaks down the difference between feeling anxious and having an anxiety disorder, explains panic attacks and how to cope through them in the moment (using skills like the stop scale, tip, grounding techniques, and deep breathing), and shares long-term strategies for managing anxiety like exposure therapy, emotion regulation, and coping ahead. she also addresses nighttime anxiety and nightmares, answers listener questions on topics like test anxiety and supporting friends, and provides crisis resources.

episodes.title: 68. How Our Mental + Physical Health Are Connected feat. Laura Martin
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by the amazing Laura Martin—a Certified IBS Nutrition Consultant and founder of Healing to Happy (an online holistic, gut-brain focused company that helps women suffering from IBS and Anxiety to get back to eating normally without fear of FODMAP's).
guests: laura martin, certified ibs nutrition consultant and founder of healing to happy
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with laura martin, a certified ibs nutrition consultant and founder of healing to happy, to talk about the gut-brain connection and how mental and physical health are intertwined. they discuss what happens to your body when you're chronically depressed or anxious—how fight-or-flight mode impacts digestion, hormones, and organs—and why healing often requires you to take radical responsibility for yourself. laura shares practical advice on building nutrition routines, why consistent meals matter more than fasting, and how to set small, achievable goals instead of overwhelming yourself. the conversation is honest about how hard it is to show up for yourself, but also how empowering it feels when you do.

episodes.title: 67. High School RECAP
episodes.excerpt: This solo episode is all about my high school experience (3 states, 3 schools, treatment—it was a wild ride folks). I dive into pre-treatment, during residential/therapeutic boarding school stays, and moving home as well as navigating COVID. I also answer loads of listener questions about…
episodes.summary: sadie recaps her entire high school experience across three states and three schools—from severe depression and suicidal ideation freshman year, through residential treatment at mclean and therapeutic boarding school in montana, to finally graduating during covid. she shares what she learned about building community, prioritizing mental health, and recognizing that grades aren't everything. she also answers listener questions on finding clubs, balancing work and school, maintaining sleep schedules, and navigating friendships. her main takeaway: high school is the best time to get mental health support, and a successful experience means looking back and feeling proud of who you became.

episodes.title: 66. Alexis Haines on Teenage Addiction, Childhood Trauma, and Taking Radical Accountability Over Your Healing
episodes.excerpt: Alexis Haines—my podcast mom—is finally on She Persisted! This episode can only be described as WOW. From teenage heroin addict, twice convicted felon, and a member of the Bling Ring to addiction center owner, an amazing mom, doula, podcast host, and more Alexis is the living proof that sobriety…
guests: alexis haines, addiction center owner, doula, podcast host, and author
episodes.summary: alexis haines talks about her path from teenage heroin addiction and being in the bling ring to over a decade of sobriety and running her own recovery center. she breaks down how drugs weren't the problem—childhood trauma and pain were—and why traditional behavioral health treatment misses the point by focusing on stopping the behavior instead of healing what's underneath. alexis explains the ace score (adverse childhood experiences), why community and unconditional love matter more than willpower, and how both big and little traumas shape us. she shares what actually keeps her grounded today: meditation, connecting with loved ones, and checking into her reality instead of escaping it.

episodes.title: 65. Therapy 101: Your Guide to Teen Treatment feat. Lindsay Fleming LPC
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Lindsay Flemming, LPC a Chicago-based therapist working to help individuals take baby-step their way to understanding & normalizing mental health.
guests: lindsay fleming lpc
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with lindsay fleming lpc, a chicago-based therapist who specializes in working with teens. they break down all the different types of therapy (outpatient, inpatient, iop, php, residential), explain what happens in your first therapy session, and talk through how to know if therapy might be right for you. lindsay also covers what teens commonly want support on, how to navigate confidentiality with your parents, how to switch therapists if it's not a good fit, and other mental health resources teens can use. this episode is designed to be a practical guide for any teen considering therapy or already in treatment.

episodes.title: 64. Inside the Secret World of the Troubled Teen Industry: Breaking Code Silence
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Sydney Montana, a TTI survivor who attended Cross Creek (a Southern Utah Behavioral Modification Program) for over 15 months.
guests: sydney montana, cross creek survivor
episodes.summary: sadie talks with sydney montana, a survivor of cross creek, a behavioral modification program in southern utah where she spent 15 months. sydney shares what led to her enrollment at 15—substance use, depression, a suicide attempt—and the traumatic intake process where she was restrained and isolated from family for months. she describes the program's strict, controlling environment: monitored constantly, unable to speak freely, punished for minor infractions, and subjected to harmful "therapy" tactics like having a rat trap placed on her leg. the conversation explores why parents choose these programs, how hard it is to heal from the experience, and why ethical, evidence-based teen mental health treatment matters so much. sydney reflects on attachment and abandonment issues she still navigates today.

episodes.title: 63. Overcoming Stagefright, Finding Your Voice, and Networking 101 feat. Rae Fung
episodes.excerpt: Rae Fung is a Speaking Coach. Impact-driven millennials and teens work with her to Own their Unique Voice and Story to be Bold, Brave and Brilliant, and never Compare themselves with others. Having been an emcee and on-screen host for 7 years, Rae has mastered the art of connecting on stage…
guests: rae fung, speaking coach
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with rae fung, a speaking coach from singapore, to talk about conquering stage fright and building confidence. rae shares how to find your unique inner and physical voice by questioning every piece of content you consume and forming your own opinions instead of conforming. they unpack the fears behind public speaking—rejection, judgment, failure—and walk through how to befriend those fears by checking if your anxious thoughts are facts or just stories. rae offers practical tips for calming nerves (like making the space familiar, moving your body to release anxious energy, and focusing on your audience instead of yourself) and breaks down networking as a value exchange where even young people have tons to offer, from tech skills to fresh perspectives.

episodes.title: 62. The Evolution of the Treatment Industry, Navigating Adolescent Addiction, and the Compassionate Care Model feat. Evan Haines
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Evan Haines. Evan is the co-founder of Alo House, a leader in the compassionate care model, and an active member in the recovery community. He works to connect with clients and help them obtain and maintain sobriety through compassion rather than control. (bio adapted from…
guests: evan haines, co-founder of alo house
episodes.summary: sadie talks with evan haines, co-founder of alo house, about his journey to sobriety after his mother's suicide when he was 14, his drunk driving arrest at 30, and finding recovery through aa. they discuss the troubling history of addiction treatment—from asylums to the violent therapeutic community model created by synanon—and why compassionate, non-controlling approaches work better than punishment. evan challenges the disease model of addiction, arguing that addiction arises from disconnection, family systems, and a sick society. they also critique wilderness therapy and the troubled teen industry, and talk about what parents and teens can do when facing addiction: find community, take responsibility for family dynamics, and seek people who won't judge or control.

episodes.title: 61. Bite Sized Mindfulness for Adolescents feat. Kira Willey
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Kira Willey. Kira works to bring music, movement, and mindfulness to kids, in lots of different ways: through her books and music, with school programs and performances, and by working with educators and parents.
guests: kira willey, mindfulness educator and children's author
episodes.summary: sadie talks with kira willey, a mindfulness educator who works with kids and adolescents through music, movement, and books. they break down what mindfulness actually is—paying attention to the present moment with kindness and curiosity—and why it matters for mental health, especially during high-stress moments like tests or social anxiety. kira shares simple, bite-sized techniques teens can use anywhere (like the stop break, starfish breath, and body scans) and explains the science behind how deep breathing calms the amygdala and helps you stay grounded. the episode ends with a guided body scan meditation you can return to anytime.

episodes.title: 60. Vulnerability, Relatability, and Empowerment feat. Zachery Dereniowski
episodes.excerpt: Today I am joined by Zachery Dereniowski (@mdmotivator) a former college dropout turned medical student and mental health advocate!
guests: zachery dereniowski, medical student and mental health advocate
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with zachery dereniowski (@mdmotivator), a former college dropout turned medical student and mental health advocate. they talk about zachery's journey from academic failure to medical school, his experiences with anxiety and overthinking during covid and a breakup, and how journaling helped him cope. the conversation covers how to support someone struggling with mental health when you haven't experienced it yourself, the power of validation over problem-solving, and how gender norms make it harder for men to express emotions and seek help. zachery shares practical tools like micro goals and diffusers (activities that make vulnerable conversations easier), and both emphasize that asking for help is the hardest and most important step.

episodes.title: 59. How to Discuss Your Mental Health in Your College Application According to a Former USC Admissions Counselor
episodes.excerpt: Today I am sitting down with Hillary Higgins, the Associate Director of College Counseling at The Nueva School and a former USC Admissions Counselor.
guests: hillary higgins, associate director of college counseling at the nueva school and former usc admissions counselor
episodes.summary: sadie talks with hillary higgins, associate director of college counseling at the nueva school and former usc admissions counselor, about navigating mental health disclosure in college applications. they discuss how to decide whether sharing your mental health journey is right for you, framing your experience in a solution-focused way that highlights growth and resilience, and addressing how mental health may have impacted your academic record. hillary also shares strategies for researching colleges and finding the right fit without visiting campus.

episodes.title: 58. Maintaining Your Mental Health Throughout The College Application Process (Navigating Rejection, Deferral, and Acceptance)
episodes.excerpt: This week I am sitting down with one of my best friends—Maya—to dive into how to maintain your mental health while navigating the college application process.
guests: maya
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with her best friend maya to talk through the emotional rollercoaster of college applications. they cover how to handle rejection, deferral, and acceptance letters without losing your sense of self-worth, plus practical strategies for managing stress and anxiety during the waiting periods. the conversation offers peer perspective on staying grounded when so much feels out of your control, and reminds listeners that your college decision doesn't define your value or future.

episodes.title: 57. How I Got Into the University of Pennsylvania (My Test Scores, Personal Statement, Supplementals, Activities, Recommendation Advice, Etc)
episodes.excerpt: This week I am sitting down to walk through my college applications. I go through my stats (GPA, SAT/ACT scores), extra-curriculars, personal statment, supplementals, and more!
episodes.summary: sadie walks through her entire university of pennsylvania application, breaking down her test scores, gpa, extracurriculars, and application strategy. she shares her complete personal statement about overcoming severe depression as a young teen, leaving home for treatment, and starting her podcast at fifteen. the episode offers practical advice on recommendation letters, supplemental essays, and how she framed her mental health journey as a strength in her application rather than hiding it.

episodes.title: 56. OCD + Exposure Therapy
episodes.excerpt: This week I am doing a solo episode all about OCD, anxiety, and exposure therapy! I walk you through how to tell if fears are justified, how to break the cycle of anxiety using evidence-based imaginative, introspective, and in vivo exposure techniques, reminisce on my OCD and anxiety treatment…
episodes.summary: sadie breaks down ocd, anxiety, and exposure therapy in this solo episode. she explains how to tell if your fears are justified versus anxiety-driven, then walks through three evidence-based exposure techniques: imaginative (visualizing feared scenarios), introspective (examining thought patterns), and in vivo (real-life practice). she shares personal stories from her own ocd and anxiety treatment and gives practical tips for applying exposure therapy to everyday life.

episodes.title: 55. Mental Health Advice for High School Students
episodes.excerpt: This week I am doing a solo episode on my mental health advice for high school students! From 504s, relationships with counselors, having a passion project, to working smarter not harder—I give all the details on what's allowed me to thrive academically while maintaining my mental health.
episodes.summary: sadie shares her personal mental health advice for navigating high school. she talks about using 504 plans and accommodations, building genuine relationships with school counselors, finding a passion project outside of academics, and learning to work smarter instead of just harder. the episode focuses on practical strategies she's used to succeed in school while protecting her mental health.

episodes.summary: this episode kicks off the mindfulness module of dbt by breaking down what mindfulness actually is and why it matters for your mental health toolkit. sadie teaches the three what skills—observe, describe, and participate—and explains the three states of mind (emotion mind, reasonable mind, and wise mind). the episode includes guided mindfulness practices so you can start applying these skills right away and begin building a foundation for the rest of your dbt work.

episodes.title: 16. DBT Education: Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (an overview)... changing problem behaviors, validating, key principles to use when combatting teenage depression and anxiety
episodes.excerpt: This DBT Overview episode covers the biosocial therapy, behavior change tactics, dialectics, and validation. I go over a recent interpersonal conflict with my sister and we troubleshoot the interaction to maximize for objective effectiveness.
episodes.summary: sadie breaks down the fundamentals of dialectical behavioral therapy (dbt), covering the biosocial model, behavior change strategies, dialectics, and validation. she walks through a real conflict with her sister to show how dbt principles work in practice, specifically focusing on objective effectiveness—getting what you want while maintaining relationships. listeners learn concrete ways to identify behaviors they want to change and how to apply dbt thinking to interpersonal conflicts.

episodes.title: 15. How do you support a friend struggling with depression and anxiety while maintaining your own mental health?
episodes.excerpt: I sit down with my best friend from home, who recounts what it was like watching me struggle, go to treatment, and come back home successfully. We discuss the societal norms that continuously stigmatize mental illness, how to support a friend who is struggling and the importance of maintaining…
guests: sadie's best friend from home
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with her best friend from home, who shares what it was like to watch sadie struggle with mental health challenges, go to treatment, and return home. they talk through the stigma around mental illness that makes it hard to support friends openly, and explore how to be there for someone who's struggling. the episode emphasizes a key lesson: you need to maintain your own mental health and support system first before you can show up for someone else.

episodes.title: 14. The effect of depression and anxiety on a family… feat. my younger sister
episodes.excerpt: In this episode, I sit down with my younger sister and we talk about how mental health impacts a family unit. We dive into her experience at home while I was at McLean, the differences she saw in me and the family, and the skills that she learned as well! We talk about the difficult spot you get…

episodes.summary: sadie sits down with her younger sister to talk about how mental health struggles affect the whole family. they discuss what it was like at home while sadie was at mclean hospital for treatment, the changes her sister noticed in sadie and their family dynamics, and the difficult position of wanting to talk about what's happening but feeling like it's not your story to share. her sister also shares dbt skills she learned through the process and offers advice on finding someone to talk to when a loved one is struggling.

episodes.title: 11. Emily Thelen (MA+LCPC+CTRS) on adjusting to change, societal norms, therapeutic boarding school, wilderness, and recovering from depression and anxiety.
episodes.excerpt: This week I sit down with one of my therapists from my therapeutic boarding school. We talk about how she saw me change, the difficulty of measuring long-term emotional change, and the societal norms of not feeling negative emotions. Emily also asks me what is important to be successful in therapy.
guests: emily thelen (ma, lcpc, ctrs)
episodes.summary: sadie sits down with emily thelen, one of her therapists from therapeutic boarding school, for a conversation about sadie's own journey through treatment. they discuss how emily witnessed sadie's changes over time, why emotional growth is hard to measure in the moment, and how society pushes us to avoid negative feelings instead of processing them. emily also turns the tables and asks sadie what she thinks makes therapy actually work.

How do we maintain our friendship as independent often dramatically different people? Do we experience relationships in the…
